Padmanav Swain And Another vs State Of Odisha And Others
.... Opp

Bench: K.R. Mohapatra, Savitri Ratho
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 W.P.(C) No.21659 Of 2025
 Padmanav Swain and Another .... Petitioners
 Mr. Srinibash Satapathy, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Odisha and others ....

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opp. Parties
 Mr. Swayambhu Mishra,
 Additional Standing Counsel
 Coram:
 Justice K.R. Mohapatra
 Justice Savitri Ratho
 Order
Order No. 06.11.2025
 04. 1.
This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. Mr. Satapathy, learned counsel for the Petitioners relied upon the case laws in Mohar Singh (dead) through Lrs and Others Vrs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others; 2023 INSC 1019 and Suresh Kumar Vrs. State of Haryana and Others; 2025 INSC 550 in which the Hon'ble Supreme Court condoned long delay in filing the Appeal under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for brevity, 'the Act').
The said case laws are not applicable in the instant case as the issue involved in this writ petition is with regard to condonation of delay in filing the application under section 64(1) of the Act. 2.1.

entities.text: Suresh Kumar Vrs. State of Haryana and Others; 2025 INSC 550
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Mr.
Satapathy, learned counsel also relied upon the case of Krishnachand and Another Vrs.

The State of Madhya Pradesh through Commissioner Jabalpur, District- Jabalpur (Jabalpur Bench of High Court of Madhya Pradesh) and Others reported in W.P.(C) No.19521 of 2017 wherein eight months delay in filing an application under section 64(1) of the Act was condoned by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh.
The second proviso to section 64(2) of the Act puts a restriction on the Collector to condone the delay in filing application under section 64(1) of the Act beyond one year.

Since there is a statutory restriction in entertaining an application under section 64(1) of the Act beyond one year, a question arises as to whether this Court has the power/jurisdiction to condone a delay of 10 years in filing an application under section 64(1) of the Act.
3.
Mr. Satapathy, learned counsel for the Petitioners prays for an adjournment to come prepare to address the issue.
